Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner announcement says its reports are fully model-generated and generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos; the individual advisory does not identify the model or scanner workflow version.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-4v2w-w6g6-f8f8 on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126071. The advisory establishes conditional thread exhaustion and does not assert exploitation.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Active Storage 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and provides patches. The fix re-raises errors after the response commits, closing the stream and releasing the thread; clients receive a truncated body and the exception reaches application error reporting.

impacts.conditions: In affected Active Storage proxy applications, if a storage-service error occurs after the response is committed, a server thread can remain blocked. Repeated failed proxy downloads can exhaust server threads; applications using only affected streaming proxy paths are in scope.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: nvm can expose NVM_AUTH_HEADER to other local users through downloader arguments
summary: When NVM_AUTH_HEADER is configured, nvm passed the credential to curl or wget as a process argument. Other local accounts may read it while nvm downloads from a private mirror. The exposure is limited to shared hosts and to the token permissions; BusyBox wget remains an exception because it cannot use a private config file.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner. Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 announcement says the opt-in scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and describes its reports as model-generated. The advisory does not identify the model or case-specific workflow.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-h3c2-g6gc-6cgx on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121745. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm now supplies curl the header on stdin and uses a private temporary WGETRC for GNU Wget. BusyBox wget still exposes the header in process arguments; the vendor advises installing curl on shared hosts when using NVM_AUTH_HEADER.

impacts.conditions: Node Version Manager (nvm) is a POSIX-compliant shell function for managing multiple node.js versions. In versions 0.40.0 through 0.40.8, when `NVM_AUTH_HEADER` is set, `nvm_download` passes the credential to curl or wget as a `--header "Authorization: ..."` command-line argument. Process arguments are visible to every local user (on Linux via `ps` or `/proc//cmdline` unless `/proc` is mounted with `hidepid=`; on macOS via `ps`), so another unprivileged account on the same machine can read the token while nvm is downloading during `nvm ls-remote`, `nvm install`, and similar commands, and gain whatever access it grants on the private mirror. Only users who set `NVM_AUTH_HEADER` on a host shared with other local accounts are affected. Version 0.41.0 passes the header to curl on stdin and to GNU Wget in a private temporary config file. BusyBox wget reads no config file, so when it is the only downloader available the header is still passed as an argument. CWE-214 Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: nvm --save can overwrite a file through a symlinked .nvmrc
summary: When nvm use or install runs with --save / -w, its .nvmrc writer followed a symlink and truncated the target file. A repository or archive can supply the symlink, but exploitation requires a user to run the save option in that directory. The maintainer documents this as an independently fixable write primitive, separate from the symlink read flaw CVE-2026-121747.
ai_role: The advisory says the issue was also found independently and earlier by Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-G9REVGKT; it separately credits the reporter. Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement establishes that the scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and generates model-produced reports. Exact model and per-case workflow are unspecified.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-8qjx-8r8m-mpqh on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121746. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 refuses to write through a symlinked .nvmrc when --save / -w is requested.

impacts.conditions: When a repository supplies .nvmrc as a symlink outside itself and the user runs nvm use --save or nvm install --save, nvm follows the link and truncates a writable target or writes the resolved version string. The CNA states attacker does not control the written content and this is data loss, not code execution.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: A symlinked .nvmrc can make nvm print a readable file
summary: nvm read .nvmrc through symlinks and could print the target file contents in an invalid-version message or version display. A repository/archive can point .nvmrc at a readable file such as .npmrc; the attacker sees output only where the victim exposes it, such as a CI log or shared terminal. The advisory says this has the same outcome as CVE-2026-94185 through a different symlink mechanism, and is distinct from the separate --save write flaw CVE-2026-121746.
ai_role: The maintainer advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-G9REVGKT) and separately names an independent reporter. Anthropic’s Oct 8 scanner announcement identifies use of its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and says reports are model-generated. The advisory does not specify which model produced this issue.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-j6ch-mq5c-3h4x on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121747. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 avoids printing the contents of a symlinked .nvmrc; users of the documented bash cd hook must also update that copied hook.

impacts.conditions: A symlinked .nvmrc can make nvm print a readable file; disclosed data is limited to text nvm emits.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: A project .npmrc can redirect nvm prefix cleanup to another file
summary: When nvm use --delete-prefix invokes npm config delete, npm reads the project .npmrc first and may edit a user-selected config file. A malicious project can cause a victim’s config file to be rewritten or left world-writable; on a shared machine that can expose file contents or permit another local user to modify it. The advisory says project code does not run and the attacker chooses the target, not written bytes.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-WYRTKBQ5). Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement says the scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and issues model-generated reports; exact model and workflow for this finding are not stated.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-ccgf-7gv4-xg5h on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121748. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 prevents project .npmrc settings from selecting the config file that npm edits during prefix cleanup.

impacts.conditions: A cloned repository/archive or local user in a writable shared parent can control project `.npmrc`; when a user runs `nvm use --delete-prefix`, npm may rewrite a selected config such as ~/.bashrc or make a global config world-writable. The attacker chooses the target but not written bytes, and no project code runs.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: A .nvmrc version can be parsed as grep options and expose local file characters
summary: nvm passed a requested version to grep without -e, allowing a version beginning with a hyphen to be parsed as grep options. The documented option combination can make GNU grep search the current directory recursively and follow symlinks; matching characters may then appear in nvm output and configured mirror request/logs. The advisory limits the readable character set and reports testing with GNU grep only; BSD and BusyBox grep were not tested.
ai_role: The advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner discovered this case as ANT-2026-EN9DM7WC. Anthropic’s Oct 8 primary announcement establishes the scanner’s model-generated reports and use of its strongest models including Claude Mythos; no case-specific model is named.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-xmxw-6r9w-89gc on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121749. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 passes version patterns to grep with -e.

impacts.conditions: With GNU grep, a crafted .nvmrc beginning with grep options and a bare nvm install, a repository symlink to .npmrc can expose the user’s npm token in terminal output and mirror/proxy logs. Disclosure is limited to 0-9A-Za-z._+- characters.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: nvm offline install can reuse a tarball that failed checksum verification
summary: A downloaded archive with a checksum mismatch remained in the nvm cache. If a user subsequently runs nvm install --offline for that version before an online retry, nvm may install the rejected archive and run its node/npm binaries. The advisory says an attacker must alter the tarball but not its separate checksum file, such as through a poisoned CDN/cache object; a mirror controlling both is outside the stated threat model.
ai_role: The advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-7NCT51FE). Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement says the scanner uses its strongest models including Claude Mythos and produces model-generated reports; exact model and workflow are not disclosed for this item.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-262q-c465-prmr on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121750. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 removes archives that fail checksum verification so offline mode cannot install them.

impacts.conditions: The CNA description states: Node Version Manager (nvm) is a POSIX-compliant shell function for managing multiple node.js versions. In versions 0.40.5 through 0.40.8, `nvm_download_artifact` downloads a release archive directly to its final path in `$NVM_DIR/.cache` and verifies its checksum afterwards; on a checksum mismatch it reports an error but leaves the rejected archive in place. A later `nvm install --offline` of the same version installs that cached file without a checksum, so an archive that was just rejected gets installed and its `node` and `npm` run. This gives code execution to a party who can alter the downloaded tarball (for example a poisoned CDN or cache object) but cannot also forge the `SHASUMS256.txt` beside it, if the victim runs `nvm install --offline` for that version after the visible "Checksums do not match" failure and before any online retry. Version 0.41.0 only puts an archive in the cache once its checksum has passed.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: nvm can evaluate malicious Node mirror version metadata as shell arithmetic
summary: nvm stored an unvalidated version field from a mirror index as an LTS alias. Later alias resolution evaluated the suffix as shell arithmetic; the advisory says bash and zsh can expand command substitutions there, allowing a malicious or compromised mirror to persist a payload that runs on later local nvm commands. A project .nvmrc path also reaches the function but is treated by the maintainers as hardening because using nvm in an untrusted project directory usually precedes running its code. The advisory explicitly distinguishes this version-field issue from earlier download-path evaluation CVEs.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner with two scanner IDs for this one underlying issue; they are not counted as two cases. Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement establishes the scanner’s use of strongest models including Claude Mythos and model-generated reports. The exact model and reason for two IDs are not specified.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-7prg-rw9c-82h7 on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121751. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 restricts arithmetic to numeric suffixes and drops invalid version rows before aliases are stored.

impacts.conditions: A malicious Node mirror version string is evaluated as shell arithmetic by nvm; only include code execution if source confirms shell-command interpretation.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: libheif can spend minutes of CPU repeatedly decoding large derived HEIF images
summary: A crafted HEIF image can make a single decode repeatedly construct oversized canvases while retaining only small crops, consuming tens of seconds to minutes of CPU in applications that decode untrusted images. The advisory reports measured reproduction, identifies no known memory-safety impact, and limits the affected range to libheif before 1.23.7.
ai_role: The libheif maintainer advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-XHT9G07S. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner page says the service scans with its strongest models, and its Oct 8 launch post identifies Claude Mythos among them. The individual advisory does not identify the model used for this report.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-48p4-gj45-w9v6 on 2026-10-26 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-XHT9G07S); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: A master fix adds a per-decode pixel budget and avoids decoding tiles outside the image; the advisory says release 1.23.7 is expected as the first patched release. The documented impact is CPU exhaustion when untrusted HEIF files are decoded; no memory-safety issue is known.

impacts.conditions: An application must decode an untrusted HEIF/derived image; source reports CPU exhaustion and successful decode of a small image.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: Trilogy#escape can permit unauthenticated SQL injection with multibyte string encodings
summary: Trilogy#escape mishandles strings in Shift_JIS, Windows-31J, Big5, GBK, and GB18030 because a multibyte continuation byte can overlap ASCII syntax. Applications are affected when attackers control the encoding of strings being escaped, or when using unsupported connection encodings. The advisory identifies unauthenticated SQL injection in affected Rails and Rack applications.
ai_role: The primary Trilogy maintainer advisory labels the report AI-assisted and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as discovering it under ANT-2026-9KOHJMNW. Anthropic’s primary scanner page says it scans with its strongest models; the Oct 8 launch post names Claude Mythos among those models. No item-specific model is stated.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-744p-w4gc-m3gh on 2026-10-29 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-9KOHJMNW); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: Trilogy 2.13.2 rejects the unsupported legacy connection encodings and fixes escaping. Projects unable to update can enforce encodings for strings passed to escape/query, as described by the advisory.

impacts.conditions: Apps are affected when attacker-influenced strings are escaped under non-ASCII-compatible encodings or the connection uses such an encoding; the advisory documents unauthenticated SQL injection in those cases but does not specify resulting reads or writes.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Caddy rewrite can decode file path information twice and bypass path-based restrictions
summary: The rewrite handler inserted a decoded file-matcher remainder without escaping it, after which the rewritten URI was percent-decoded again. On configurations using try_files, split_path, and a rewrite with that remainder, a double-encoded path can bypass an earlier path-based deny matcher and expose static files; reserved characters can also alter the path or query. The advisory demonstrates the behavior and limits applicability to that configuration pattern.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-32RAL55Q. Anthropic’s primary scanner page describes an AI model-based scanning service and the Oct 8 launch post identifies Claude Mythos among its strongest models. The item-specific model is unspecified.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-69hv-5jfc-mvmv on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-32RAL55Q); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 escapes the file-matcher remainder while preserving slashes before parsing the rewritten URI.

impacts.conditions: Requires the Caddy rewrite/try_files configuration using the file remainder placeholder; attacker supplies crafted path info.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: SoftFileLock stale-lock breaking can remove a live marker after inode reuse
summary: The stale-lock breaker closes its marker after checking the inode and timestamp, allowing a filesystem that immediately reuses inode numbers to make a later live marker appear stale. Another local user able to create files in the lock directory can force the race, unlinking the live marker so two processes enter the same protected section without warning. The advisory reports the race on ext4, xfs and overlayfs over them; tmpfs, btrfs, a single contender and StrictSoftFileLock are not affected.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory says Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) reported the finding on Oct 15, identifies ANT-2026-KIIS96IX, and says maintainers reviewed it. The public advisory appeared Oct 17. Anthropic’s primary scanner program page establishes model-based scanning; no specific model is identified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-fq56-3cx3-fjxp on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-KIIS96IX). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep soft locks in a directory other local users cannot write, use tmpfs, or prefer native FileLock where available; StrictSoftFileLock is unaffected. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: Race may remove a live stale-lock successor after inode reuse, admitting two simultaneous lock holders; mutual exclusion failure only.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: A crafted filelock ReadWriteLock database can make every acquire hang
summary: SQLite loads the full schema at each ReadWriteLock acquire, while the timeout only bounds lock waits. Another local account able to place or replace the database file can provide a small crafted schema that stalls acquires while allocating about 1 GB, or makes them loop at full CPU indefinitely. The effect is availability only; the advisory specifies the writable/replacable database-path precondition and affected filelock versions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-NFPRHMYJ, gives the finding title and severity, and records maintainers’ review. Its event history says it was split from a group draft into an individual issue. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; the model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-cwqr-hh33-gh44 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-NFPRHMYJ). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep the lock database and its parent directories writable only by the locking account, and do not share a writable database across accounts. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: A local user able to replace the SQLite lock database can supply a crafted schema that makes ReadWriteLock acquisition stall or hang; initial/per-acquisition exposure varies by affected version.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: filelock can adopt a lock protocol directory created by another user
summary: StrictSoftFileLock and SoftReadWriteLock accept an existing protocol directory after checking only that it is a directory, not who owns it. Another local user who creates the derived directory before the lock user’s first acquire can remove claims, admit concurrent holders, redirect lock-user writes, or hold acquire/release beyond its timeout. The advisory identifies the pre-creation condition and affected versions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory states Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-Q5VK5JEE and logs that four other scanner IDs were moved to separate advisories, so this row maps to one individually described issue. The advisory says maintainers reviewed it. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; the exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-9c4x-gm8v-wgc4 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-Q5VK5JEE). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep lock protocol directories in a location other accounts cannot write. Where a shared directory is necessary, pre-create and verify the protocol tree as the service user. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: In a shared parent directory, another local user can create/adopt the protocol directory first and alter protocol state so concurrent holders are admitted; this violates the lock protocol. No further impact is established.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: filelock ReadWriteLock can follow planted SQLite side files and alter lock-user files
summary: SQLite reopens the lock database by name and processes adjacent journal, WAL and shared-memory side files. Another local account able to create or rename entries in the database directory can make the lock user’s ordinary lock operation write attacker-chosen bytes to the lock user’s files, create or unlink files, admit conflicting readers/writers, or kill a holder. The advisory narrows affected versions and describes how sticky directories reduce but do not remove all denial-of-service variants.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner with ANT-2026-KMJ2575J and gives the per-finding issue description. It records the scanner report date and maintainers’ review. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; no model is identified for this case.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-v4x8-3wr5-3wq8 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-KMJ2575J). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep the lock database in a directory only the locking account or root can write, and do not share a writable database across accounts. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: On POSIX, attacker needs rename access in a non-sticky parent to swap database/side-file names. Attacker-chosen content overwrite additionally requires a writable adjacent hot journal; the description also states overwrite or unlink operations.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: StrictSoftFileLock claim directories can let another user remove a live hold
summary: StrictSoftFileLock creates the directories containing claim files with bare mkdir calls, so a permissive umask or default ACL can leave them writable by another local user despite a restrictive lock-file mode. That user can unlink the 0600 claims; a later contender then enters while the original holder believes it still holds the lock. The advisory documents the required permission settings and says the common 022 umask without permissive ACLs does not allow the unlink.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) with finding ANT-2026-AD6SUOON, provides a reproducer, records maintainer review, and states that this issue was split from a grouped draft into its own advisory. The report was received Oct 15; the public advisory was published Oct 17. Anthropic’s scanner page establishes AI-model provenance; exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainer published GHSA-6627-m3xw-93mp on Oct 17, 2026 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-AD6SUOON). The internal scanner report was received Oct 15; that report date is retained in evidence and is not used as public attribution date.
remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue. Use restrictive umask, avoid default ACLs that grant other users write access to claim directories, and keep strict locks in directories other accounts cannot write. Existing .filelock trees may need permission correction after upgrade.

impacts.conditions: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From version 3.30.0 until version 4.2.1, StrictSoftFileLock and AsyncStrictSoftFileLock on POSIX systems create coordination and claim directories without applying the caller’s restrictive lock mode. A permissive umask or inherited default ACL can leave these directories writable by another local user, allowing that user to delete an active holder’s claims. Another authorized process can then acquire the lock while the original holder remains in its critical section. An attacker can also plant malformed claims to prevent acquisition. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1. CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: StrictSoftFileLock can follow a symlink swapped in after its directory check
summary: StrictSoftFileLock checks the coordination directory with lstat, then later uses the path by name. Another local user able to rename the directory can exchange it for a symlink between those operations, causing the lock-user process to create claim files in a directory the attacker chooses. This can strand claims that deny another strict lock or make multiple holders enter a critical section. The advisory limits the issue to POSIX-style conditions and lists the relevant shared-directory and pre-created-link cases.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) with finding ANT-2026-SVFEYX89, provides a scanner reproducer, records maintainer review, and states this was split from the grouped advisory. The report was received Oct 15; the public advisory was published Oct 17. Anthropic’s scanner page establishes AI-model provenance; exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainer published GHSA-m462-7rxw-wvpg on Oct 17, 2026 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-SVFEYX89). The internal scanner report was received Oct 15; that report date is retained in evidence and is not used as public attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep strict locks in directories other users cannot write. In sticky shared directories, create and verify the lock directory as the service account before other users can claim it. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.30.0 until 4.2.1, On POSIX platforms, StrictSoftFileLock and AsyncStrictSoftFileLock validate the coordination directory in _ensure_protocol_directory but later reach the claims directory through _open_directory by pathname, allowing a local account that can rename the coordination name to swap in a symbolic link between check and use during acquisition. That race can create and leave claim files in another writable directory or strand claims in a different strict lock so the second lock times out. Separately, the claims property and force_break follow a resting symbolic link without a race when the lock user inspects or recovers the lock. Claims inspection discloses a file name to the other account only if the resulting exception text or claim_name reaches that account through a shared log, CI output, or error report. A blind force_break recovery that removes live claims from another strict lock can allow two processes into that lock's critical section; this path reaches other strict locks, not arbitrary files. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1. CWE-363: Race Condition Enabling Link Following
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: SoftFileLock symlink swapping can disclose whether a private path exists or is writable
summary: During SoftFileLock acquire, the writability check first uses lstat and then os.access, which follows symlinks. A local user able to change entries in the lock directory can swap a marker for a symlink between these calls. The different acquire outcomes reveal one bit indicating whether a chosen path exists or is writable by the lock user; the lock does not open, create, or modify the target through the symlink. Linux fs.protected_symlinks blocks the leak in a sticky world-writable directory such as /tmp, but not in a writable non-sticky or sticky group-writable directory.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this privately as ANT-2026-RQ91AXTW, includes the reproducer and maintainer review, and assigns CVE-2026-112912. The advisory was publicly published Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance. No model is specified.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-9j6q-wvj5-jgjg on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-RQ91AXTW). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: Use a lock directory writable only by the lock account, or a Linux sticky world-writable directory with fs.protected_symlinks enabled. Do not use soft locks as root in directories other accounts can write. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

impacts.conditions: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.32.6 until 4.2.1, SoftFileLock can follow a swapped symbolic link during the conditional os.access writability check for a node without its owner-write bit, allowing another local user on a platform and directory configuration that follows the link to infer whether a chosen path exists and is writable from the observable acquisition result. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1. CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: SoftReadWriteLock can write through a replaced holder record and block lock operations
summary: SoftReadWriteLock refreshes holder records by reopening a path and writing without checking the opened file type. A different local user who owns or can write the lock’s .rw tree can replace a record with a FIFO, making waiting acquires hang beyond timeout and blocking a holder heartbeat so a second process can enter while the first still believes it holds the lock. Where the OS permits cross-owner hard links, it can also make the lock user overwrite the first roughly 135 bytes of one of its own private files with the holder record. The FIFO issue works on default Linux; the hard-link variant has additional OS policy requirements.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-AT33VEVC, includes the scanner’s reproducer and maintainer review, and assigns CVE-2026-112934. The advisory was published Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-fj95-fr6c-h845 on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-AT33VEVC). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.

title: SoftFileLock stale-break restore can follow a swapped symlink and link a private file into the lock directory

The attacker can read metadata and retain a name for the file, and a subsequent FileLock open can truncate or change permissions on the linked file. The advisory limits the affected behavior to specific race conditions, platforms and filelock versions; a sticky directory on tested settings is not affected.

remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 fixes the stale-break restore path. Keep soft locks out of directories other local users can write without the sticky bit, and do not take a native FileLock on a path another user controls.

Apache credits Anthropic’s OSS Scanner report ANT-2026-MAPKT6MZ as first reported to its security team on Oct 26, 2026, then separately credits Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research for a Nov 3 report. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
ai_role: Apache’s primary vulnerability ledger explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as finder of this CVE under ANT-2026-MAPKT6MZ and dates its security-team report before the independent Google report. The official Anthropic OSS Scanner page identifies the service as periodic security scans by Anthropic’s strongest models. Specific model and internal steps for this finding are not public.
classification_note: Apache published the security entry and fix with httpd 2.4.71 on Nov 11, 2026. Anthropic reported privately on Oct 26; Apache publicly names that attribution in the release advisory. Apache labels the issue critical and says it can lead to RCE; no claim of exploitation is made.
remediation_note: Apache fixed the issue in httpd 2.4.71 by updating mod_http2 assign_headers() to write into the request headers table. Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or the vendor’s fixed package; deployments should also check standalone mod_h2 releases. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: The source states the mod_http2 race can lead to RCE; further prerequisites are not established in this description.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: LibreOffice dBASE index import heap buffer overflow and recursive-page handling flaw
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; separately reported by an anonymous TrendAI Zero Day Initiative participant
summary: When reading a dBASE index page, LibreOffice did not constrain the recorded entry count to the page capacity; crafted pages could trigger a heap buffer overflow. A page could also refer to itself and recurse without end. LibreOffice credits Claude and says Anthropic found the issue using agents studying open-source project security; Ada Logics validated and reported it. A separate anonymous TrendAI ZDI reporter is also credited.
ai_role: The primary LibreOffice security advisory states “found by Anthropic using agents to study the security of open-source projects” and credits Claude; it says Ada Logics validated and reported. It separately acknowledges an anonymous TrendAI ZDI report, so AI discovery credit applies as one credited discovery among independent reports.
classification_note: The official LibreOffice advisory announced the vulnerability on Nov 5, 2026 and credits Claude/Anthropic. No claim of exploitation is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in LibreOffice 26.2.6 and 26.8.1. The project recommends upgrading to either fixed branch. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted dBASE index can cause a heap buffer overflow; a self-referential page can recurse during index handling. Specific consequence beyond these effects is not established.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: Xen grant-copy cache validation flaws permit cross-domain arbitrary memory read and write
organization: Anthropic and Xen Project; validated by Ada Logics; independently reported by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team
summary: Incorrect revalidation of cached grant-copy details can mix frame numbers and grant references (CVE-2026-102703), or place the check restricting frame-number copies to caller-owned memory incorrectly (CVE-2026-102704). Xen’s primary advisory says a malicious guest can read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other domains, including Dom0. The two CVEs are separately identified manifestations in one XSA-523 underlying grant-copy cache-validation issue, so this record counts the shared discovery once.
ai_role: The signed primary Xen advisory explicitly says the issue was discovered by Anthropic using Claude, then validated by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics; it also notes an independent report by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team.
classification_note: XSA-523 was publicly released Nov 3, 2026. The advisory explicitly separates the two CVE manifestations but presents them as one grant-copy validation issue; they are grouped here as one distinct discovery. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Apply the appropriate attached XSA-523 patches to the relevant Xen stable branch. The advisory lists no known mitigation. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A malicious guest can read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other Xen domains, including Dom0. CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704 share this XSA impact statement; apply to both exact CVEs.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

impacts.conditions: A malicious guest can read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other Xen domains, including Dom0. CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704 share this XSA impact statement; apply to both exact CVEs.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Pillow JPEG draft scaling leaves unchecked lossless output geometry and overflows decode buffer
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; python-pillow maintainers
summary: Pillow’s JPEG draft/thumbnail path sizes a row buffer for a downscaled image. With lossless SOF3 JPEG supported by libjpeg-turbo 3.x, the decoder ignores the requested scaling and returns full-width scanlines; Pillow does not verify the actual output geometry before decoding. The scanline write therefore exceeds the heap buffer. The advisory reports attacker-controlled overflow bytes, but does not establish arbitrary code execution. It affects paths using draft before load; decoder builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject this format before the bug.
ai_role: The primary Pillow security advisory explicitly states the issue was found by Anthropic using Claude to study open-source software and manually validated by Ada Logics. The model version is not identified.
classification_note: The advisory was publicly published Oct 17, 2026, and specifies a 90-day coordinated disclosure window. It rates the issue High. No exploitation claim is made; the reported overflow primitive is not summarized as RCE.
remediation_note: Fixed in Pillow 13.0.0. The advisory notes that loading before thumbnailing or setting reducing_gap=None avoids the affected draft path; builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg are not affected. Upgrade to the fixed Pillow release. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: CNA description: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Zephyr RTIO syscall verifier reverses user-buffer memory permission checks
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; Zephyr Project maintainers
summary: In `rtio_vrfy_sqe()`, permission-check results from `K_SYSCALL_MEMORY()` were accumulated with the wrong polarity. On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_RTIO, an unprivileged user-mode thread with an RTIO context and iodev grant could supply a pointer to kernel memory; the verifier accepted it and a driver dereferenced it in supervisor mode. The advisory describes arbitrary kernel reads through TX, writes through RX, or a kernel fault.
ai_role: The primary Zephyr advisory explicitly says Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, discovered the vulnerability; Ada Logics performed manual triage and report writing with Anthropic Research.
classification_note: The public GHSA was published Nov 4, after the stated Nov 2 embargo. It rates the issue High. Exploitability requires a user-mode thread already granted RTIO access and an image built with CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_RTIO. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in Zephyr 4.3.2 and 4.5.0, with backports merged for v4.4, v4.3 and v3.7 branches. The advisory recommends rejecting nonzero K_SYSCALL_MEMORY results and checking TXRX transmit buffers read-only. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A user-mode thread granted an RTIO context/device can submit pointers to arbitrary kernel memory; RTIO RX can write peripheral data to chosen kernel memory and TX can transmit kernel memory over the bus.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: Mastodon statistics endpoints compute expensive queries before enforcing admin authorization
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; Mastodon maintainers
summary: An instance statistics endpoint intended for administrators performed expensive statistics computation before checking that the requester had the required permission. Anonymous requests could therefore trigger long-running SQL queries and quickly exhaust server resources. The advisory states this is a denial-of-service issue and provides fixed release versions.
ai_role: The primary Mastodon GHSA explicitly attributes discovery to Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, and states Ada Logics manually triaged and wrote the report in collaboration with Anthropic Research.
classification_note: The project published the GHSA Jul 27, 2026; severity High (CVSS 7.5). The issue is anonymous request-driven resource consumption; no exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in Mastodon 4.4.21, 4.5.14, 4.6.4 and 4.7.0-alpha.2. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: Before authorization is checked, anonymous callers can send repeated parameterized requests that trigger long-running admin-metrics SQL queries and exhaust server resources.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Gitea pre-receive hook reuses a branch permission check across refs in one push
organization: Anthropic Research and Doyensec; Gitea maintainers
summary: Gitea caches a positive permission check for one branch and reuses it while processing later refs in the same multi-ref push. A user with a legitimate per-branch maintainer-edit grant could include another protected ref and have the stale authorization reused, allowing writes beyond the granted branch, including protected branches and tags. The advisory reports this on Gitea 1.25.5.
ai_role: The primary Gitea advisory states Claude found the initial bug and wrote the exploit where applicable; a Doyensec researcher reviewed and personally confirmed the reproduction.
classification_note: The advisory was republished at the project’s request on Jun 21; it explicitly preserves the original private-submission timeline beginning Apr 16 for the coordinated-disclosure window. It identifies 1.25.5 as affected and 1.26.3 as patched.
remediation_note: The advisory recommends evaluating CanMaintainerWriteToBranch for every ref rather than caching the result across the push batch. Fixed version listed: Gitea 1.26.3. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A per-branch maintainer permission is reused across refs in a single push, granting full repository write access beyond the branch-specific grant.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: PrestaShop back-office listing filter names allow SQL injection beyond employee permissions
summary: Back-office listing filter names were insufficiently validated before being incorporated into database queries. A logged-in employee could submit a crafted filter name to read data outside their profile’s permissions, including employee password hashes and customer and order tables. The advisory states the reporter demonstrated the issue with the most restricted built-in profile.
ai_role: The primary PrestaShop advisory explicitly says Claude (Anthropic) discovered the vulnerability as part of Anthropic’s coordinated disclosure program; Doyensec verified it and reported it to the project.
classification_note: The public advisory has GHSA-whxq-pxj5-qq7v but no CVE assigned. It rates the issue Moderate (CVSS 6.5); exploitation requires a logged-in employee. Older 1.7.x and earlier versions are stated to be end of life and unpatched.
remediation_note: Upgrade supported installations to PrestaShop 9.1.5 or 8.2.8. No workaround is given. The same flawed legacy back-office controller is also present in 1.7.x and earlier, which the project says are end of life and will not be patched.

impacts.conditions: A logged-in employee crafts a back-office list filter; even the most restricted built-in profile can read arbitrary shop database data, including employee hashes, customer and order tables.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: Pillow tiled TIFF decoder reads beyond short tile buffers while unpacking rows
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; python-pillow maintainers
summary: Pillow’s tiled TIFF decoder allocates a tile buffer according to libtiff’s reported tile size, then iterates and unpacks rows as if the buffer held the full worst-case tile. An undersized returned tile can therefore make the `copy4` unpacker read beyond the allocation. A crafted TIFF can crash the process and may cause adjacent heap memory to be copied into decoded pixels.
ai_role: The primary Pillow advisory explicitly says Anthropic found the issue using Claude and Ada Logics helped validate and report it; the report says the data was reviewed manually.
classification_note: The public GHSA rates it Moderate (CVSS 6.5). The advisory describes denial of service and possible adjacent-memory disclosure into decoded pixels; it does not claim code execution.
remediation_note: Fixed in Pillow 13.0.0. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted tiled TIFF can make Pillow copy beyond short tile allocation and expose adjacent heap data in the loaded image.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: FreeRDP shadow server divides by zero after a client acknowledges a future frame ID
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; FreeRDP maintainers
summary: The shadow server stores a client-supplied frame acknowledgment without checking that it is no greater than the last frame sent. A connected viewer can acknowledge a future frame ID; unsigned subtraction wraps, and the next frame calculation divides by zero, terminating the shadow server and disconnecting viewers. The advisory states this affects availability only and, in the default setup, the attacker must already be authenticated as a desktop viewer.
ai_role: The primary FreeRDP advisory explicitly says Anthropic found the issue using Claude and Ada Logics manually validated it. It includes a reproduction and the coordinated disclosure attribution.
classification_note: The advisory is GHSA-6vjv-4hm3-6698 and states no CVE is assigned. It rates the issue Moderate. The default configuration requires an already-authenticated connected desktop viewer. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in FreeRDP 3.32.0. Upgrade to that release or later. Deployment status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A client already authenticated to view the shared desktop acknowledges frameId+1; SIGFPE terminates freerdp-shadow-cli and drops all concurrent viewers. Availability only; source says no out-of-bounds access.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: curl HTTP/2 upload reset triggers use-after-free
product: curl and libcurl HTTP/2 upload handling
ai_system: Claude (reporter credited as “Luna with Claude”; exact model/version not specified)
summary: During an upload, a server RST_STREAM with HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED or REFUSED_STREAM can cause curl to use a freed Curl_easy object. The curl project says remote code execution has been demonstrated only under a long list of strict heap, version, architecture, TLS, parallel-transfer, and timing conditions; the advisory rates it High and does not assert exploitation in the wild.
ai_role: The primary curl advisory credits “Luna with Claude, Anthropic” as the reporter of this exact flaw. The public source establishes Claude-assisted reporting/discovery attribution, but does not describe the model’s internal discovery process or identify a specific model version.
classification_note: Counts as an AI-attributed discovery because the project advisory explicitly credits Luna with Claude as reporter; no claim of autonomous discovery or exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or the fixed maintenance releases (8.20.2, 8.16.2, or 8.14.3 in their respective branches), apply the upstream patch, or avoid HTTP/2. Confirm the installed libcurl version because applications may bundle or dynamically link it.

impacts.conditions: During an upload, curl mishandles HTTP/2 `RST_STREAM` received from the server (with reason `HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED` or `REFUSED_STREAM`) leading to a use after free of a `struct Curl_easy` object. CWE-416 Use After Free
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: Xen grant-table version changes leave stale status-page pointers
summary: A v2→v1→v2 grant-table version change can free and reallocate status pages while retaining previously calculated pointers into the status array. Xen says an unprivileged guest may gain host privileges; information leaks and denial of service are also possible. The issue affects x86 guests allowed to use grant table v2 on multi-vCPU guests; Arm is unaffected.
ai_role: Xen’s signed XSA-517 explicitly says the issue was discovered by Claude Opus and diagnosed as a security issue by Teddy Astie of Vates.
classification_note: One XSA/CVE and one underlying grant-table race finding. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Apply the appropriate XSA-517 patch for the supported Xen stable branch. The advisory gives temporary mitigations `gnttab=max-ver:1` on the hypervisor or `max_grant_version=1` in guest configuration. Restricting grant-table v2 avoids this condition but changes guest-visible configuration; use the vendor patch where available.

impacts.conditions: XSA-501 was about issues with v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1 changes racing certain other grant table operations. Sadly a v2 -> v1 -> v2 change has yet another effect which wasn't accounted for: During the first change, status pages would be freed. During the second change they would be allocated again. Hence across the full pair of change the addresses of the status pages may change, rendering stale previously calculated pointers into the status array.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: Xen VM entry failure with branch tracing can crash HVM/PVH guests
summary: With branch tracing enabled, a special combination of intercepted #DB, single stepping, and STI/MovSS blocked state can still trigger fatal VM entry failure. Xen says HVM/PVH guest userspace code may crash the guest, causing denial of service. Affected hardware is Intel, VIA, or Zhaoxin VMX; Arm, AMD, and Hygon are not affected, and PV guests cannot exploit it.
ai_role: Xen’s signed XSA-518 explicitly says the issue was discovered by Claude Opus and diagnosed as a security issue by Teddy Astie of Vates.
classification_note: Distinct from XSA-517/CVE-2026-79610: this is a VMX branch-tracing guest denial-of-service condition with a separate patch. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Apply the attached XSA-518 patch for Xen 4.17.x through 4.20.x or Xen unstable/4.21.x, as applicable. The advisory lists running only PV guests, or HVM guests only on AMD/Hygon hardware, as mitigations; these change deployment choices and are not substitutes for patching affected Intel/VIA/Zhaoxin systems.

impacts.conditions: With branch tracing enabled and the specified intercepted #DB/single-step/STI-or-MovSS state, fatal VM entry failure can crash an HVM/PVH guest on affected hardware.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not establish exploitation in the wild.

title: Podman image annotation can disable requested container sandboxing
product: Podman container creation from OCI checkpoint images
organization: ADA Logics Ltd; Anthropic; Podman maintainers
summary: Podman treated an image carrying `io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name` as a checkpoint and could ignore user-supplied sandbox settings such as `--cap-drop=ALL`, instead applying checkpoint-controlled container settings. The Podman maintainers removed this behavior. The advisory says rootless containers are not affected because they do not support checkpoint/restore.
ai_role: The primary Podman advisory explicitly credits ADA Logics Ltd with discovering this vulnerability using Anthropic’s Claude models. This is item-specific model-assisted discovery attribution; the source does not identify the Claude model/version.
classification_note: Counts once as the single finding tracked by GHSA-2cvf-wqm6-wr9g and CVE-2026-94603. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Podman 5.8.8 or 6.1.3 or later. The maintainers reverted checkpoint handling through `podman run`. As an interim safeguard, reject pulled images carrying the checkpoint annotation; rootless containers are not affected according to the advisory.

impacts.conditions: When a rootful podman run processes an image with the checkpoint annotation, it ignores supplied restrictions such as --cap-drop=ALL; image-controlled checkpoint state can select weaker sandbox settings and capabilities. Rootless containers are unaffected. This documents a sandbox restriction bypass; no specific resulting privilege gain or host compromise is established.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Libreswan IKEv2 EAP state machine null dereference permits unauthenticated DoS
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; Libreswan Project
summary: An inconsistent IKEv2 state-machine fall-through dereferences a null EAP state pointer on an IKE_AUTH packet, even when EAP is not configured. A remote unauthenticated peer can repeatedly trigger daemon crashes and restarts; the project explicitly says remote code execution is not possible.
ai_role: The primary Libreswan security alert credits “Claude by Anthropic, as reported by David Korczynski from ADA Logics Ltd.” This is explicit attribution for this exact CVE; the source does not identify a Claude version or describe the discovery process.
classification_note: One pre-authentication denial-of-service finding. The vendor explicitly rules out remote code execution; no exploitation-in-the-wild claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Libreswan 5.3.3 or 5.4.1 or later, depending on branch, or apply the vendor patch. The advisory says malicious unauthenticated IKE_AUTH packets can repeatedly crash/restart `pluto`; verify downstream package versions.

impacts.conditions: A malicious IKE_AUTH packet reaches Libreswan's affected IKEv2 state machine; authentication and configured EAP are not required. Repeated crashes and restarts of pluto can deny service; the CNA explicitly excludes remote code execution.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: Botan TLS ASIO stream use-after-free may expose heap data
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (service documented to use Anthropic’s strongest Claude models; exact model/version not identified)
summary: A use-after-free in Botan’s TLS ASIO integration can disclose heap data to a peer, depending on the application’s usage pattern. The Botan advisory limits exposure to applications using `botan/asio_stream.h` with simultaneous reads and writes outstanding.
ai_role: The primary Botan advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner under item ID ANT-2026-4PMK7FYH. Anthropic’s official OSS Scanner page says its periodic scans use its strongest models and describes the service as informed by its experience using Claude. The specific model and internal analysis steps for this finding are not public.
classification_note: The vendor release notes say fixed in Botan 3.14.0, dated Nov 4; the linked public vendor handbook that records the scanner credit is dated Nov 6. Scope is limited to ASIO TLS stream applications with concurrent reads/writes.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Botan 3.14.0 or later. Only applications using the ASIO TLS stream API are in scope; applications should review their use of concurrent reads/writes. Botan says disabling TLS 1.2 is only a partial, not complete, countermeasure.

impacts.conditions: In Botan TLS ASIO integrations using `botan/asio_stream.h`, a use-after-free may leak heap memory to the peer depending on application use patterns.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Botan TLS 1.3 handshake buffers unbounded dummy ChangeCipherSpec messages
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (service documented to use Anthropic’s strongest Claude models; exact model/version not identified)
organization: Anthropic; Trail of Bits/OpenAI; Tencent Keen Security Lab; Botan authors
summary: Before a TLS 1.3 server determines whether to downgrade to TLS 1.2, it buffered incoming ChangeCipherSpec messages. An unauthenticated peer could send many dummy CCS messages to pin unbounded memory during the handshake and cause denial of service. Botan’s advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner and also credits Trail of Bits in collaboration with OpenAI and Tencent’s SecBuddyF; the shared underlying bug is counted once.
ai_role: The primary Botan advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner under item ID ANT-2026-5QKEFF4F for this exact TLS 1.3 memory-consumption finding. Anthropic’s official OSS Scanner page describes periodic scans using its strongest models and says the service is informed by its experience using Claude. The specific model and analysis steps are not public. Other organizations are also credited on the same finding, so this record counts the bug once and does not claim exclusive discovery.
classification_note: One TLS 1.3 handshake memory-exhaustion finding with multiple credited research organizations. Botan fixes it in 3.14.0. The public vendor guide with the scanner credit is dated Nov 6; the release notes are dated Nov 4.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Botan 3.14.0 or later. The release notes also describe a configurable limit on consecutive useless TLS records (default 32), but use the fixed release rather than assuming a custom limit mitigates every affected code path.

impacts.conditions: An unauthenticated peer can send many dummy ChangeCipherSpec messages during a TLS 1.3 handshake and pin unbounded memory.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: Libreswan FIPS certificate parsing assertion permits pre-authentication daemon DoS
product: Libreswan IKEv1/IKEv2 certificate processing in FIPS mode
summary: In FIPS mode, Libreswan asserts that `CERT_ExtractPublicKey()` returned a key. A malformed X.509 certificate with an invalid public key can make the function return NULL and crash the daemon. An unauthenticated peer can send the CERT payload before authentication and repeatedly cause denial of service. The vendor explicitly says no remote code execution is possible. Exposure requires both the OS and Libreswan to run in FIPS mode and at least one CA certificate to be loaded.
ai_role: The primary Libreswan alert states the project used Claude to audit its codebase and that Claude found this vulnerability; it credits Claude as finder and Guillaume Winter as reporter.
classification_note: Vendor states no RCE and gives exact FIPS/CA-certificate preconditions. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Libreswan 5.3.2 or later, or apply the vendor patch. The only workaround described is disabling FIPS mode, which may violate deployment requirements. Scope requires FIPS mode at both OS and Libreswan and a loaded CA certificate; repeated unauthenticated CERT payloads can crash the daemon.

impacts.conditions: In FIPS mode, Libreswan's add_decoded_cert() function calls CERT_ExtractPublicKey() and asserts that the result is not NULL. However, CERT_ExtractPublicKey() returns NULL when public key extraction fails, for example if the RSA exponent is set to 0. A remote attacker can send a malformed X.509 certificate in a CERT payload to trigger the assertion, causing the pluto daemon to abort and restart. Continued exploitation causes a denial of service. No remote code execution is possible. Both IKEv1 and IKEv2 are affected. The vulnerability is only exploitable when both the OS and libreswan are running in FIPS mode and at least one CA certificate is loaded. The CERT payload is processed before peer authentication, so no credentials are needed to exploit this. Configurations using only PreSharedKey (PSK) authentication with no CA certificates loaded in the NSS database are not vulnerable. CWE-617: Reachable Assertion CWE-252: Unchecked Return Value
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: iperf3 server frees streams while remote-triggered worker threads may still use them
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; ESnet iperf maintainers
summary: In the server timer path, stream objects could be freed while per-stream worker threads were still live, allowing a remote heap use-after-free. The fix marks streams done and cancels/joins worker threads before freeing them. The release and fixing commit attribute discovery to Claude/Anthropic and Ada Logics validation/reporting.
ai_role: The primary upstream fixing commit says the issue was “found by Anthropic using agents to study the security of open-source projects,” with Ada Logics validating and reporting. It maps finding ANT-2026-E5BA80X9 directly to CVE-2026-101283.
classification_note: Upstream release errata says CVE labels in the two fix commit messages were interchanged; the fixing commits themselves unambiguously map this server-side use-after-free to CVE-2026-101283 and ANT-2026-E5BA80X9. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to iperf3 3.22 or later. The patch cancels and joins stream worker threads before freeing their streams. This applies to the affected server code; verify downstream packages include the fix.

impacts.conditions: iperf3 3.20–3.21 (esnet/iperf) has a pre-auth heap buffer overflow in decrypt_rsa_message(): a 256-byte RSA buffer is BIO_read with the attacker-controlled ciphertext length (guard warns only), so an unauthenticated client overflows the heap via an oversized authtoken; fixed in 3.22 CWE-122 Heap-based buffer overflow
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: iperf3 authentication RSA decryption accepts ciphertext longer than its output buffer
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; ESnet iperf maintainers
summary: The RSA authentication decrypt path could process an encrypted input longer than the output buffer sized to the RSA modulus, risking heap buffer overflow. The fix rejects ciphertext lengths greater than the RSA output size rather than continuing with the read. The upstream commit attributes discovery to Anthropic’s agents and reporting/validation to Ada Logics.
ai_role: The primary upstream fixing commit says this was “found by Anthropic using agents to study the security of open-source projects,” with Ada Logics validating and reporting. It maps finding ANT-2026-FXH14FHV directly to CVE-2026-101276.
classification_note: Upstream release errata says CVE labels in the two fix commit messages were interchanged; the fixing commits themselves unambiguously map the `iperf_auth.c` heap overflow to CVE-2026-101276 and ANT-2026-FXH14FHV. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to iperf3 3.22 or later. The patch rejects encrypted input longer than the RSA modulus-sized output buffer. Verify downstream packages include the fix.

impacts.conditions: iperf3 3.21 (esnet/iperf) contains a remote, unauthenticated heap use-after-free: the server's per-test watchdog server_timer_proc() frees streams without cancelling/joining their worker threads, so a blocked worker dereferences a freed iperf_stream; fixed in 3.22.
impacts.exploitation: The cited source does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.

title: NSD IP range ACL comparison can allow unintended addresses on little-endian systems
product: NLnet Labs NSD IP-range access controls
organization: Claude/Anthropic; Ada Logics; NLnet Labs; Qifan Zhang (Palo Alto Networks)
summary: On little-endian systems, NSD compared IP addresses and ACL ranges using host-endian values even though the values were in network byte order. Addresses meant to be denied could therefore be allowed. The vendor fixed the comparison in NSD 4.15.1. The official CVE record credits both Qifan Zhang and Claude/Ada Logics as finders. Its timeline states Qifan reported the issue and received a private patch before the later Claude/Ada report; the public advisory appeared only when the fix released. The available sources do not establish whether the Claude report independently rediscovered the privately known issue, so this record preserves the collision caveat without claiming first discovery.
ai_role: The primary NLnet Labs advisory thanks Qifan Zhang, Claude and Ada Logics for discovering and responsibly disclosing this exact vulnerability. title: Big Sleep finds a QuickJS BigInt out-of-bounds read
summary: An off-by-one digit calculation in BigInt string conversion can read past the allocated BigInt structure. The QuickJS upstream changelog lists release 2025-09-13 as the next release; no exploit claim is made.
ai_role: The Google-assigned CVE record credits Google Big Sleep as finder and references the individual Google Issue Tracker report (434193024). The sources do not specify human review steps.
classification_note: The public Google-assigned CVE record attributes the finder and lists versions before 2025-09-13 as affected; no exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Google CNA record identifies versions earlier than QuickJS 2025-09-13 as affected; the upstream changelog confirms that release date. The changelog itself only summarizes miscellaneous bug fixes, so no specific commit is identified here.

impacts.conditions:
CNA description: A vulnerability exists in the QuickJS engine's BigInt string conversion logic (js_bigint_to_string1) due to an incorrect calculation of the required number of digits, which in turn leads to reading memory past the allocated BigInt structure.

  *  The function determines the number of characters (n_digits) needed for the string representation by calculating:

$$ \\ \text{n\_digits} = (\text{n\_bits} + \text{log2\_radix} - 1) / \text{log2\_radix}$$

$$$$This formula is off-by-one in certain edge cases when calculating the necessary memory limbs. For instance, a 127-bit BigInt using radix 32 (where $\text{log2\_radix}=5$) is calculated to need $\text{n\_digits}=26$.


  *  The maximum number of bits actually stored is $\text{n\_bits}=127$, which requires only two 64-bit limbs ($\text{JS\_LIMB\_BITS}=64$).


  *  The conversion loop iterates $\text{n\_digits}=26$ times, attempting to read 5 bits in each iteration, totaling $26 \times 5 = 130$ bits.


  *  In the final iterations of the loop, the code attempts to read data that spans two limbs:

C



c = (r->tab[pos] >> shift) | (r->tab[pos + 1] << (JS_LIMB_BITS - shift));









  *  Since the BigInt was only allocated two limbs, the read operation for r->tab[pos + 1] becomes an Out-of-Bounds Read when pos points to the last valid limb (e.g., $pos=1$).


This vulnerability allows an attacker to cause the engine to read and process data from the memory immediately following the BigInt buffer. This can lead to Information Disclosure of sensitive data stored on the heap adjacent to the BigInt object.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

impacts.conditions: The CNA description states: A type confusion vulnerability exists in the handling of the string addition (+) operation within the QuickJS engine. * The code first checks if the left-hand operand is a string. * It then attempts to convert the right-hand operand to a primitive value using JS_ToPrimitiveFree. This conversion can trigger a callback (e.g., toString or valueOf). * During this callback, an attacker can modify the type of the left-hand operand in memory, changing it from a string to a different type (e.g., an object or an array). * The code then proceeds to call JS_ConcatStringInPlace, which still treats the modified left-hand value as a string. This mismatch between the assumed type (string) and the actual type allows an attacker to control the data structure being processed by the concatenation logic, resulting in a type confusion condition. This can lead to out-of-bounds memory access, potentially resulting in memory corruption and arbitrary code execution in the context of the QuickJS runtime.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

ai_role: GHSL credits an AI agent it developed, reviewed by Man Yue Mo and Peter Stöckli. GHSL records the report on 2026-01-05 and links the vendor advisory.
classification_note: The public advisory documents the vulnerability and disclosure/remediation status. It does not claim exploitation in the wild.

impacts.conditions: CNA description: Open WebUI is a self-hosted artificial intelligence platform designed to operate entirely offline. Prior to 0.8.6, there is a vulnerability in chat completion API, which allows attackers to bypass tool restrictions, potentially enabling unauthorized actions or access. In the chat_completion API, the parameters tool_ids and tool_servers are supplied by the user. These parameters are used to create a tools_dict by the middleware. This is then used by get_tool_by_id to retrieve the appropriate tool. However, there is no checks in that ensures the user that uses the API has permission to use the tool, meaning that a user can invoke any server tool by supplying the correct tool_id or tool_servers parameters via the chat completion API. Moreover, the authentication token stored in the server would be used when invoking the tool, so the tool will be invoked with the server privilege. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.8.6.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: GHSL AI-agent index lists wim security descriptor off-by-one read in 7-Zip
ai_system: GitHub Security Lab AI agent (system not named in advisory)
summary: The WIM security descriptor handler performs an off-by-one heap read while parsing a crafted security descriptor.
ai_role: GHSL’s primary AI-agent index lists this 7-Zip advisory as discovered with AI agents; the individual disclosure credits Jaroslav Lobačevski but does not describe an agent or item-level AI contribution. The named system/model is therefore unknown; no claim of independent AI discovery is made.
classification_note: The cited sources document the issue and fix but do not claim exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Fixed in 7-Zip v26.01 released 2026-04-27. The advisory identifies an off-by-one heap over-read in WIM SecurityId parsing.

impacts.conditions: The CNA description states: 7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio. Versions 9.34 through 26.00 contain an off-by-one heap out-of-bounds read in the WIM (Windows Imaging) archive handler's security descriptor lookup. In CHandler::GetSecurity (CPP/7zip/Archive/Wim/WimHandler.cpp), the per-image SecurOffsets table holds numEntries + 1 cumulative offsets, but the check securityId >= SecurOffsets.Size() admits securityId == numEntries, and the function then reads SecurOffsets[securityId + 1], fetching one UInt32 past the end of the heap-allocated CRecordVector (which performs no bounds checking on operator[]). The securityId is attacker-controlled at offset +0xC of any directory entry in WIM metadata, and the handler is registered for .wim, .swm, .esd, and .ppkg and enabled by default in stock 7z.dll; the OOB triggers zero-click in the GUI because 7zFM.exe's ListView calls GetRawProp(kpidNtSecure) for every item during listing (ASan-confirmed), and is also reachable via CLI listing with 7zz l -slt. Impact is limited to denial of service under hardened allocators and minor information disclosure, since the OOB value is only consumed arithmetically as a length and is not surfaced to the attacker; there is no write primitive.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: GHSL AI-agent index lists NTFS compressed-stream heap overflow in 7-Zip
ai_system: GitHub Security Lab AI agent (system not named in advisory)
summary: An undefined 32-bit shift can under-allocate the NTFS compressed-stream buffer to one byte; reading attacker-controlled compressed data can then overflow the heap.
ai_role: GHSL’s primary AI-agent index lists the advisory among findings discovered with AI agents. The individual advisory credits Jaroslav Lobačevski but does not specify an agent or per-finding contribution; attribution is index-level only.
classification_note: The advisory documents a proof of concept and potential impact, with no claim of exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Fixed in 7-Zip v26.01 released 2026-04-27. On 64-bit systems the 8 GB secondary allocation may fail on lower-memory systems, limiting impact there.

impacts.conditions: CNA description: 7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio. Versions 26.00 and prior contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability caused by an under-allocation in the NTFS compressed stream buffer (GetCuSize shift UB), potentially allowing attackers to cause arbitrary code execution or application crashes. CInStream::GetCuSize() in the NTFS handler computes the compression-unit buffer size as (UInt32)1 << (BlockSizeLog + CompressionUnit), and a crafted image with ClusterSizeLog >= 28 and CompressionUnit == 4 drives the exponent to 32, which is undefined behavior and collapses on x86/x64 so _inBuf is allocated as 1 byte. ReadStream_FALSE then writes up to 256 MB of attacker-controlled data into that 1-byte buffer in 64 KB iterations, and because the CInStream object sits only 304 bytes after _inBuf, its vtable pointer is overwritten and the next dispatched call achieves a vtable hijack. On 32-bit builds the overflow is unconditionally reached; on 64-bit it requires the parallel 8 GB _outBuf allocation to succeed, otherwise failing closed to denial of service. The NTFS handler is enabled by default in stock 7z.dll and, via signature-based fallback matching "NTFS    " at offset 3, will open a crafted image regardless of file extension during extraction or testing. Version 26.01 fixes the issue.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.

title: FreeBSD thr_kill2 sends signals despite a failed permission check
summary: The syscall did not check the result of p_cansignal() before sending the signal, permitting unauthorized signals across users or jail boundaries.
ai_role: FreeBSD credits the Tsinghua team using GLM-5.1 and a human reporter. The advisory states multiple parties independently reported the issue before publication; no priority claim is made.
classification_note: The cited sources document the vulnerability and remediation; they do not claim exploitation in the wild.
